preconditions.description: The first line of input is a positive integer T representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(len(row) == M for row in [input().strip() for _ in range(T)]) and all(len(row) == N for row in [input().strip() for _ in range(T)])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first line is a string of length M (1 ≤ M ≤ 10^5) representing terminal row outcomes, and the second line is a string of length N (1 ≤ N ≤ 10^5) representing terminal column outcomes.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(Q, int) and Q >= 0 for Q in [int(input()) for _ in range(T)])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the third line is a non-negative integer Q (1 ≤ Q ≤ 10^5) representing the number of queries.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= N and 1 <= y <= M for x, y in [tuple(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(Q)] for _ in range(T))
preconditions.description: Each query consists of two integers x and y (1 ≤ x ≤ N, 1 ≤ y ≤ M) representing the initial position of the stone.

postconditions.expression: stdout == ''.join(['1' if (x + y) % 2 == 1 and (x == 0 or y == 0) or (x + y) % 2 == 0 and (x == 0 or y == 0) else '0' for x, y in queries])
postconditions.description: For each query (x, y), the output is '1' if Alice wins (i.e., the initial position (x, y) is a winning position for Alice) and '0' if Bob wins, based on the game's rules and terminal conditions.

postconditions.expression: all(len(output) == Q for output in [stdout.split()[i] for i in range(T)])
postconditions.description: The output for each test case is a string of length Q, where each character corresponds to the result of a query.

postconditions.expression: all(output[i] in ['0', '1'] for i in range(Q) for output in [stdout.split()[i] for i in range(T)])
postconditions.description: Each character in the output string is either '0' or '1', representing Bob's or Alice's win, respectively.
